{"action":"shell","command":"python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='/testbed/specs/001-transactions/spec.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='## Requirements *(mandatory)*'
assert anchor in s
edge='''- TTL on replacement: re-putting an existing key with `ttl=None` clears any
  prior expiry (entry becomes immortal); re-putting with a finite TTL sets a
  fresh absolute expiry computed from the current `timer()` value (the prior
  expiry is never extended or reused).
- `ttl=0`: the entry is expired at insertion time; it is never observable via
  `get`, `len`, or invalidation, and it occupies no effective capacity in
  observable state (it is purged before any operation).
- Exact expiry boundary: at `timer() == timer_at_put + ttl` the entry is
  expired (comparison is inclusive); just before that instant it is live.
- Invalid TTL values: negative numbers, `bool` (`True`/`False`), non-numeric
  types, and non-finite numbers (infinity, NaN) all raise `ValueError` before
  any state change; `ttl=None` is always valid.
- Expired entry with tags: its tag memberships are removed at purge time, so
  later invalidation of that tag counts only live entries.
- Purge ordering: expiry purging happens before the requested operation and
  does not reorder or otherwise touch the recency of surviving entries; a
  `get` that follows a purge still refreshes the hit entry\'s recency as usual.
- `timer` argument: any callable returning a number is accepted; the default
  (`timer=None`) is the standard monotonic clock; the timer is consulted only
  for expiry decisions and never mutates caller state.
- Backward compatibility: caches and `put` calls that never use `timer`/`ttl`
  behave exactly as before milestone 3 (no expiry, no clock reads required for
  observable behavior).

'''
s=s.replace(anchor, edge+anchor, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok edges inserted')
PYEOF"}
